sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display of the tagged construct was confirmed (construct described as 'surface-displayed tagged TRPC5'); no channel-function assay (e.g. Ca2+ flux or patch-clamp) is reported for this specific DogTag construct in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: The ledger clip (L1) explicitly names the junction as between Y460 and N461 of full-length human TRPC5; Python confirms seq[459]='Y' and seq[460]='N', matching the paper exactly. Position 460 falls within the extracellular loop ECL3 (landmarks 455–476), 6 residues from the TM4 C-boundary (454) and 16 residues from the TM5 N-boundary (477), satisfying the ≥3-residue clearance on both sides. No cysteine is present in ECL3; the N461-G-S sequon is disrupted by the insert but the paper explicitly validated this construct for surface display. Full-length human TRPC5 with DogTag (DIPATYEFTDGKHYITNEPIPPK) flanked by GGGGS linkers inserted between Y460 and N461 by site-directed mutagenesis; construct co-expressed with SYFP2 in HEK cells and used to characterise surface-displayed TRPC5. [validation: surface_only; position: validated; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: For pcDNA4-TRPC5-DogTag-SYFP2, DogTag (underlined), flanked by a glycine-serine linkers (GGGGS DIPATYEFTDGKHYITNEPIPPK GGGGS) was introduced between Y460 and N461 of human TRPC5 by site-directed mutagenesis with Q5 High-Fidelity DNA polymerase (NEB).

literature_notes: L2 and L3 both describe a C-terminal SYFP2 fusion of full-length human TRPC5. The topology landmarks place the C-terminus (residue 973) firmly in the intracellular region (625–973); this tag is therefore on the cytoplasmic face and does not qualify as an extracellular surface tag. L2's functional data (EC50 ~15 nM, comparable to untagged TRPC5) pertains to this intracellular-tagged construct and cannot be used to propose or validate an extracellular site. Only L1 grounds an extracellular insertion, yielding one site.
